top_choice_rationale: P001 (Melitz and Helpman, B048) is the only awardable proposal on the slate and the one I prefer on discovery, maturity and attribution. Melitz (2003) is an identifiable originating model of selection into exporting and reallocation across firms. Its qualitative predictions (exporter premia, selection, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) have been tested in firm-level data over more than twenty years, and Helpman's exporting-versus-FDI work with Melitz and Yeaple makes the two-name credit coherent. The main residual risk is priority for Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and a citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism handles it adequately. Welfare-gain magnitudes depend on functional form, so the citation should not claim more than the mechanism. Awarding P001 is clearly better than no award. I do not rely on the number of supporters as evidence of merit.
recusal_note: No connection to Melitz or Helpman is apparent from my profile. I disclose, without adjudicating, long-term co-authorship and IIES ties with committee colleagues John Hassler (chair) and Timo Boppart (co-opted member), and that I am committee secretary. My field is heterogeneous-agent macroeconomics, which is adjacent to macro uses of heterogeneous-firm models but not to trade itself.
